text:
alice: FYI ran into a weird duplicate processing case while testing the batch endpoint with our onboarding sample. Repro steps in local: enqueue job -> SDK refreshes token mid-request -> server returns 429 -> client retries and job runs twice.

ryan: thanks. is this with streaming=false or streaming=true?

alice: batch API, streaming=false. The SDK's retry hot path assumes idempotent handlers. Our sample job does a webhook call that isn't idempotent.

lin: do we have any guards in the sample? idempotency-key? dedupe on server side?

alice: neither. sample was kept tiny for clarity.

ryan: can you paste sanitized logs?

alice: logs: 
```
[2026-04-02T08:12:03Z] DEBUG client: start request req=job-709
[2026-04-02T08:12:03Z] INFO  auth: token expired, refreshing
[2026-04-02T08:12:03Z] WARN  transport: 429 during refresh-retry req=job-709
[2026-04-02T08:12:03Z] DEBUG client: retrying immediate req=job-709
[2026-04-02T08:12:04Z] INFO  webhook: delivered job-709 (attempt=1)
[2026-04-02T08:12:04Z] INFO  webhook: delivered job-709 (attempt=2)
```

lin: immediate retry after refresh seems bad. We should add a tiny randomized backoff if the last action was a token rotation. Also make sample send Idempotency-Key: job-<id>.

ryan: Agreed. Two-prong fix: 1) sample-level idempotency header by default, 2) SDK: add optional "replay_guard" behavior that does small jittered backoff when 429 follows token refresh. off by default but enabled in sample.

alice: I'll add the header and a short README section describing why sample enables it.

lin: we also need a unit test that simulates a refresh race and asserts webhook called once. Could be a flaky test if timing is naive; suggest a deterministic fake clock in tests.

ryan: +1 on fake clock. Also track telemetry metric: dx.replay_guard.blocked_duplicates (emit only request id). No payload data.

alice: created draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/sampleapp/pull/502 (includes idempotency header + test harness).

lin: we should also update SDK parity matrix: node/python currently differ for streaming semantics on 429 (node delays, python retries immediately). Open parity issues so we don't ship asymmetry.

ryan: opened issues: https://go/redwood/issues/SDK-PARITY-701 (node/python streaming-vs-batch retry behavior).

alice: small note for docs: add a Troubleshooting snippet to onboarding that shows how to reproduce safe-replay locally using the included simulate-429 script. developers keep hitting this when they copy-paste sample without idempotency.

lin: for runtime folks: if replay-guard becomes common we might add a server-side dedupe by req-id for webhook endpoints as a belt-and-suspenders approach. I'll ping eng-runtime.

ryan: timeline?

alice: patch tonight, tests tomorrow, enable in staging sample canary Thursday.

(dx-bot): linked PR 502 to ticket DX-847 and added label "dx/replay-guard".

lin: one more: document SDK config option names clearly. I propose client.init({ replayGuard: { enabled: false, jitterMs: [20,200] } })

ryan: sounds good. ensure defaults don't increase latency too much for high-throughput users. make it tunable.

alice: will include performance note and microbenchmark numbers in PR description.

ryan: thanks all, feel free to merge sample PR once tests pass. I'll shepherd the SDK parity issues after lunch.
